articles.title: What is new: Shine Lens, Material brushes, Symmetry and smoother first steps
articles.summary: New in this version: the Shine Lens, Select > Material..., the Material / Spec menu brushes, the Car menu, and first-step fixes such as the guide layers being left out of your render, plus the Text button, smart guides, gradient colour stops, Refine Edge, Brush Dynamics and crash recovery for your layers.
articles.what: This page lists the newest tools and where to find them. The Shine bar under the Live Preview shows your finish under a studio light. Select > Material... selects everything made of the same finish. The Material / Spec menu (U or Shift+U) has the Material Brush, Spec Brush, Wear Brush and Spec Eyedropper. The Car menu has Mirror Paint, Mirror To Other Side and Car Stripe. The first-step fixes make Shokker easier the first time you use it. Everyday tools got better too: a Text button (T), smart guides and arrow nudge in Move, gradient presets and colour stops, Refine Edge in the Mask menu, Brush Dynamics next to Flow, and a restore prompt that brings your layers back after a crash. Newer still: the Car menu also has Number Kit (the car number on both doors and the roof), Sponsor Kit (one logo on many parts at the same real size) and Car-Space Fade (a fade along the car). Spec Doctor in the Material / Spec menu checks the spec map for mistakes. The selected-layer card is now an icon row with a More menu, and the boxes that ask for a name are Shokker’s own dialogs. Since 2026-10-10 the car tools sit in the Car menu (once called Symmetry) and the Material / Spec menu (once called Material). New: Auto Spec (a first spec for every layer), Race Wear Studio (a worn-car layer in one click) and Colourway Studio (one livery in many colourways). Spec Sculpt is now a panel and Shokk Drop has three columns.
when: You are looking for what changed or where a new tool lives.
how: 1. Shine Lens: look under the Live Preview for the Shine bar (Off, Lens, Full, Sweep). Hold the ` key for a quick peek.
2. Select > Material...: open the Select menu, click the car and press OK.
3. Material / Spec menu (next to Retouch, or press U / Shift+U): Material Brush, Spec Brush, Wear Brush and Spec Eyedropper.
4. Car menu: Mirror Paint, Mirror To Other Side, Copy To Other Side (Text Reads Right) and Car Stripe....
5. Top row: Open Paint... holds Layered template and Flat image, and Source Paint and iRacing Car Folder are now file chips.
6. First-step fixes: see the sections below.
7. Everyday tools: Text button (T), smart guides in Move, the Colours button in Gradient, Mask > Refine Edge..., the Dynamics button next to Flow. After a crash, reopen the same file and restore.
8. Tonight’s tools: Car > Number Kit..., Sponsor Kit... and Car-Space Fade..., Material / Spec > Spec Doctor, the icon row and More menu on the layer card, and in-app name boxes.
tips: Every tool here is one Ctrl+Z away from undone.
pitfalls: These tools change what you see in Shokker. Press RENDER to write the result into your paint and spec files.

articles.title: Text tool (T): type words that stay editable
articles.summary: The Text tool (T) types lettering straight onto the paint, on a layer of its own. The text stays live, so you can click it again with the Text tool to change the words, font, size, colour or alignment.
articles.what: Press T or click the Text button in the tool row (it sits right after Erase). Click the paint where the words go and type. Enter commits the text and Shift+Enter starts a new line. The tool options bar holds Font, Bold, Italic, Letter spacing, Text transform (As Typed, UPPERCASE, lowercase, Capitalize), Text alignment and Text effect (Drop Shadow, Outer Glow, Emboss, Neon). The text stays live until you rasterize it with the RASTERIZE button on its layer card, or paint over it with a brush. Move (V) on a live text layer moves the whole layer, and a double-click on it with Move opens it for editing. Scaling or rotating keeps the text live; stretching, flipping or skewing turns it into pixels. A saved project and the crash recovery both keep live text.
when: You want a driver name, a number, a slogan or a sponsor line without leaving Shokker.
You need to change the words or the font of lettering you typed earlier.
You want a glow, shadow, emboss or neon look on lettering.

2. Choose the Font, Bold, Italic, Letter spacing, Text transform, Text alignment and Text effect in the tool options bar.
3. Click the paint where the lettering goes and type. Enter commits it; Shift+Enter starts a new line.
4. To change it later, click the text again with the Text tool and edit the words or the options. With Move (V), a double-click does the same.
5. Move the whole text layer with Move (V), and use Transform (Ctrl+T) to scale or rotate it. Press RASTERIZE on its layer card only when you want plain pixels.

deep.heading: Live text versus pixels
deep.body: Live text is kept as words plus its settings, so Shokker can redraw it sharply and let you change the words, font, size, colour, alignment and effect at any time. Pixels are just a picture of the letters. Rasterize, painting over the text, stretching, flipping and skewing all turn live text into pixels. When that happens Shokker tells you, and Ctrl+Z takes you back to the live text. Use pixels only when you want to brush on the lettering or distort it.

deep.heading: Moving and editing
deep.body: Move (V) treats a live text layer as one object. Dragging anywhere on it, even in the gap between two words, moves the whole layer. A double-click on the text with Move opens the editor with the words already filled in, and Esc closes it without changes. With the Text tool, one click on existing text edits it instead of starting a new line of text.

deep.heading: Options that change the look
deep.body: Font picks the typeface. Bold and Italic add weight and slant. Letter spacing opens up or tightens the gaps. Text transform shows the same words as typed, in UPPERCASE, in lowercase or Capitalized without retyping. Text alignment sets left, centre or right for several lines. Text effect adds Drop Shadow, Outer Glow, Emboss or Neon. All of them stay editable while the text is live.

faq.a: Click it again with the Text tool, or double-click it with Move (V). The words and the options come back so you can change them.

faq.q: What does RASTERIZE do?
faq.a: It turns live text into plain pixels, like a picture of the letters. You can then brush on it, but you can no longer change the words. It is the button on the text layer card.

faq.q: Why can I not edit my text any more?
faq.a: A brush stroke over it, a stretch, a flip, a skew or RASTERIZE made it pixels. Press Ctrl+Z straight away to get the live text back.

faq.q: Does a saved project keep my text editable?

articles.title: Smart guides and arrow-key nudge: line things up exactly
articles.summary: While you move a layer or a piece of artwork, it snaps to the canvas edges and centre, to the other layers and to your selection, and coloured guide lines show what it lined up with. Arrow keys nudge a layer 1 pixel, or 10 with Shift.
articles.what: Move (V) now has smart guides. As you drag a layer or an isolated piece, its edges and centre are pulled to the edges and centre of the canvas, to the edges and centre of every other visible layer and to the active selection box. A magenta line means it lined up with another layer, a cyan line with the canvas and a yellow line with your selection. The pull is small and the same at every zoom level. Hold Ctrl to move freely with no snapping, or Shift to move in a straight line (guides are off then). Esc or letting go clears the lines. In the Move tool the arrow keys nudge the layer 1 pixel, and Shift+Arrow nudges 10 pixels. A burst of key presses is one undo step. A locked layer says it is locked instead of moving.
when: You want a sponsor or number centred, or lined up with another layer.
A logo is one or two pixels off and the mouse is not precise enough.
You want to slide something in a perfectly straight line.
how: 1. Pick Move (V) in LAYER mode and select the layer.
2. Drag the artwork. When a coloured line appears, it has snapped: magenta to another layer, cyan to the canvas, yellow to your selection.
3. Hold Ctrl while dragging to turn the snapping off for a free move, or hold Shift to move in a straight line.
4. For the last pixel, tap the arrow keys: 1 pixel each, or Shift+Arrow for 10.
5. Press Ctrl+Z if you do not like it; one nudge burst is a single undo step.

controls.effect: Move freely with no snapping.

controls.label: Shift while dragging
controls.effect: Move in a straight line.

controls.label: Arrow keys
controls.effect: Nudge the layer in the Move tool.

tips: iRacing tip: the cyan guide marks the middle of the whole 2048 x 2048 sheet, not the middle of the car. For the true centre line of the car, snap to the Wire layer outlines or use Car > Car Stripe.
To put two sponsors the same distance from a door edge, snap the first one to the edge, then snap the second to the first.
The guides only appear while you drag a layer or an isolated piece. They are never part of the paint and never render.
pitfalls: The guides snap to the visible layers only. A hidden layer is ignored, and so are the guide layers you have switched off.
Ctrl switches the snapping off. If something will not snap, check that you are not holding Ctrl.

deep.heading: What it snaps to
deep.body: The edges and centre of the moving piece are compared with the canvas edges and centre, with the edges and centre of every other visible layer, and with the box around the active selection. If any of them is within a few screen pixels, the piece is pulled onto it and a guide line is drawn with small end ticks on both objects. The pull is measured in screen pixels, so it feels the same zoomed in or out.

deep.heading: Free move, straight move and nudge
deep.body: Ctrl (or the Windows or Command key) moves without any snapping. Shift locks the move to a straight line and turns the guides off. The arrow keys nudge in the Move tool: Arrow is 1 pixel and Shift+Arrow is 10 pixels. Keys pressed in one burst count as one undo step. This works on a whole layer and on a piece that is open in a transform.

deep.heading: Which kind of move gets the guides
deep.body: Dragging an isolated piece of a layer and dragging a whole layer (hold Alt with Move) both get the guides. A live text layer is always moved as a whole layer.

faq.q: What do the pink, cyan and yellow lines mean?
faq.a: Magenta means your piece lined up with another layer, cyan with the canvas edge or centre, and yellow with your selection box.

faq.q: How do I move without snapping?
faq.a: Hold Ctrl while you drag.

faq.q: How do I move in a straight line?
faq.a: Hold Shift while you drag. The snapping guides are off while you do.

faq.q: How do I move something by exactly one pixel?
faq.a: In the Move tool, press an arrow key. Shift+Arrow moves 10 pixels.

faq.q: Is the cyan line the middle of my car?

mistakes.fix: Let go of Ctrl, show the other layer and drag closer.

articles.title: Gradient tool: fades with your own colours, presets and stops
articles.summary: The Gradient tool (G) paints a fade across a layer. The Colours button opens a gradient editor with presets and colour stops, so you can make a three-colour fade or a chrome sweep, and the fade previews live while you drag.
articles.what: In LAYER mode, pick Gradient with G (Shift+G switches between Gradient and Fill) or from the Retouch menu. In the tool options bar, next to Linear and Reverse, the Colours button opens the "Gradient colours" editor. It has preset chips (Foreground to Background, Foreground to Transparent, Black to White, Chrome sweep, Red, White, Blue bands, Sunset, Ocean, Carbon Heat, Fire, Gunmetal Fade, Midnight Candy, Lime Pop, Cobalt, Hot Pink and Gold), and a colour bar. Click the bar to add a colour stop and drag a stop to move it. For the selected stop you can set the Stop colour, its Position, its Opacity and the Midpoint to next stop, or use Delete stop. The Foreground and Background buttons link a stop to your current colours. Reverse flips the fade, Save preset keeps your own, and Reset goes back to Foreground to Background. Drag on the canvas to paint: the real gradient previews live and applies when you let go. It works with Linear, Radial, Reflected, Diamond and Conical, and stays inside an active selection. The Gradient tool runs across the flat sheet, so the left and right sides of the car and the hood, roof and trunk can come out different. For a fade that matches on the real car, use Car > Car-Space Fade....
when: You want a fade from one colour into another, or through three or more colours.
You want a chrome-looking sweep or a hard-edged band of colours.
You want a fade that goes from a colour to see-through.
how: 1. Pick LAYER mode, select a layer and choose Gradient (G).
2. Choose the shape: Linear, Radial, Reflected, Diamond or Conical.
3. Click Colours, then pick a preset chip, or click the colour bar to add stops and set each Stop colour and Position.
4. Drag across the layer where the fade should run. It previews live while you drag.
5. Let go to apply it. Ctrl+Z removes it. Use Save preset to keep a fade you like.

tips: iRacing tip: the paint sheet is the car cut open, so a fade that runs across the whole sheet breaks where one panel ends and the next begins on the car. Select the hood (or roof, or one side) first, and run the fade inside it.
For a fade into the base paint, use Foreground to Transparent so the layer underneath shows through.
A chrome look in the paint needs the matching shine as well: set the finish for that area to a mirror metal, and use the Shine Lens to check it.
pitfalls: The editor changes the Gradient tool only. The old two-colour fade from the Foreground to the Background colour is still the default preset.
Stops that follow the Foreground or Background change when you change those colours, so a saved preset with linked stops changes with them.
A long, gentle fade can show stair-steps in the sim. The Colours ramp adds dither against that; see the banding article for more fixes.

deep.heading: How the stops work
deep.body: A gradient is a list of colour stops along a line from 0 to 100 percent. Each stop has a colour, a Position and an Opacity. Between two stops the colour blends smoothly, and the Midpoint to next stop moves where the halfway colour sits. Two stops at the same position make a hard edge, which is how the Red, White, Blue bands preset gets its sharp bands. Two stops always stay, so you cannot delete the last two.

deep.heading: Live preview and smoothness
deep.body: While you drag, the real gradient is drawn over the layer or the selection, so what you see is what you get when you let go. A little dither is added so long, soft fades do not show visible bands.

deep.heading: Foreground and Background stops
deep.body: The Foreground and Background buttons link the selected stop to your current colours. The default preset, Foreground to Background, uses both links, so swapping colours with X flips the fade the next time you paint.

faq.q: Where do I change the gradient colours?
faq.a: Pick Gradient (G), then click the Colours button next to Linear and Reverse in the tool options bar.

faq.q: How do I add a third colour?
faq.a: Open Colours and click the colour bar where the new colour should sit. Then set its Stop colour.

faq.q: How do I make a fade that ends in nothing?

mistakes.symptom: The fade has a visible edge where one panel ends
mistakes.cause: The sheet is the car cut open, so panels are not next to each other like on the car.
mistakes.fix: Select one panel and run the fade inside it.

protips: Save the fades you like as presets, named after the car or the sponsor, so a team livery can reuse the same colours on every car.

articles.title: Refine Edge: make a selection follow the real edge of a logo or number
articles.summary: Refine Edge (Mask menu) cleans a rough selection so it follows the true edge of a logo or number, with a live preview. It can also make a Cut-out layer and clean the colour fringe, instead of the old guess-and-feather.
articles.what: Open the Mask menu and choose Refine Edge... (under Smooth Edges). The "Refine Edge" panel has a View row (Red overlay, On white, On black, Mask only), an Edge radius slider, a Smart radius (soft and sharp edges) tick box, sliders for Smooth, Feather, Contrast and Shift edge, and an Apply to choice: Selection or New layer (cut-out). A tick box, Clean the edge colours of the cut-out, removes the old background colour from the soft edge. Changes show live. Nothing is final until you press Apply, Cancel throws it away and Reset puts the sliders back. Applying to the selection is one undo step like Grow, Feather or Smooth.
when: A rough selection around a sponsor logo or number keeps a halo of the old background.
A cut-out logo has a white or dark fringe on the new paint.
Grow, Shrink and Feather cut into the logo or leave background behind.
how: 1. Make a rough selection around the logo or number with the Rectangle (M), Lasso (L) or Wand (W).
2. Open the Mask menu and click Refine Edge....
3. Raise Edge radius until the red overlay hugs the logo. Tick Smart radius for soft or fuzzy edges. Use the View buttons to check On white and On black.
4. Tune Smooth, Feather, Contrast and Shift edge. Choose Selection, or New layer (cut-out) to get the logo on a layer of its own, and tick Clean the edge colours of the cut-out.
5. Press Apply. Ctrl+Z undoes it in one step.

controls.effect: How far from your selection edge it looks for the real edge.

controls.label: Smart radius (soft and sharp edges)
controls.effect: Uses a wider search at soft areas and a narrow one at sharp areas.

controls.effect: Where the result goes.

controls.effect: Removes the old background colour from the soft edge.

tips: iRacing tip: a logo cut out of a photo or a white sticker sheet often carries a light fringe that shows on coloured paint. Use New layer (cut-out) with Clean the edge colours, then move the clean logo onto the car.
Check the View: On black before you apply, because a dark paint shows any leftover bright fringe.
It only works on edge areas, so large selections stay fast.
pitfalls: In a perfectly flat colour area no tool can see an edge that is far from your selection. If the edge is outside the search band, raise Edge radius.
The older Feather and Grow buttons are still there. Use them when you do not care about the picture underneath.

deep.heading: What it does that Feather cannot
deep.body: Grow, Shrink and Feather move the edge by a fixed amount whatever the picture looks like. Refine Edge looks at the picture in a narrow band around your selection edge and snaps the edge to where the colour really changes, so a sloppy selection ends up on the logo outline. Smart radius also keeps sharp corners sharp and soft areas soft.

deep.heading: Clean the edge colours
deep.body: The soft rim of a cut-out still carries a bit of the old background colour. When you tick Clean the edge colours of the cut-out, that rim is pushed toward the nearest solid logo colour, so the logo has no light or dark halo on any paint colour.

deep.heading: Selection or cut-out
deep.body: Selection replaces your selection with the refined one, so other tools use it. New layer (cut-out) leaves your selection alone and puts the logo on a new layer, which you can move, scale and mirror.

faq.q: Where is Refine Edge?
faq.a: In the Mask menu, as Refine Edge..., under Smooth Edges.

faq.q: What is the difference between Refine Edge and Feather?
faq.a: Feather blurs the edge by a fixed amount. Refine Edge looks at the picture and moves the edge to where the logo really ends.

faq.q: Does it change my paint?
faq.a: Only if you press Apply. Applying to Selection changes the selection, and New layer (cut-out) adds a layer. Cancel does nothing.

faq.q: How do I get rid of the white edge around my logo?
faq.a: Choose New layer (cut-out) and tick Clean the edge colours of the cut-out.

faq.q: Can I undo it?
faq.a: Yes. Ctrl+Z undoes it in one step, for both Selection and the cut-out layer.

mistakes.cause: The real edge is farther away than the Edge radius.
mistakes.fix: Raise Edge radius, or redo the rough selection closer to the logo.

mistakes.symptom: The cut-out still has a light edge
mistakes.cause: Clean the edge colours of the cut-out is not ticked.
mistakes.fix: Tick it and apply again.

protips: Do the rough selection one or two pixels outside the logo, not inside. Refine Edge can pull the edge in, and a selection that starts inside the logo has nothing to pull from.

articles.title: Brush Dynamics: speckle, spray, splatter and tapered strokes
articles.summary: The Dynamics button next to Flow opens "Brush dynamics", which makes every dab of the layer Brush a little different. Pick a preset like Speckle, Mud splatter, Dust and overspray or Taper out, or mix your own.
articles.what: In LAYER mode with the Brush (B), the Dynamics button sits next to Flow in the tool options bar. It opens the "Brush dynamics" panel with preset chips and a live preview of the stroke. Presets: Natural hand, Speckle, Mud splatter, Dust and overspray, Confetti, Two-tone flecks, Taper out, Taper in, and Off. Sliders: Size jitter and Smallest dab; Scatter, Dabs per step and Count jitter; Flow jitter; Taper length and Taper end size, with Grow instead of shrink and Fade the paint too; and Colour: FG / BG mix, Hue jitter, Saturation jitter, Brightness jitter, with New colour for every dab. Some presets also set Spacing or Hardness, and a toast tells you. Your choice is remembered. Shift-click a second point for a straight line that keeps the taper. Undo, opacity and selections work exactly like a normal stroke.
when: You want speckles, dust, spray or mud splatter by hand.
You want a stroke that gets thinner and ends in a point, like a swoosh.
You want random colours or sizes in a stroke.
how: 1. Pick LAYER mode, select a layer and choose the Brush (B).
2. Click Dynamics, next to Flow, to open the Brush dynamics panel.
3. Click a preset chip. Speckle and Dust and overspray read best with a small brush (size 6 to 14).
4. Tune the sliders if you like. The preview shows the effect of the stroke, not its real size.
5. Paint. Click Reset in the panel (or the Off chip) to go back to the plain brush.

controls.effect: Opens the Brush dynamics panel.

controls.effect: Throws dabs off the stroke line.

tips: iRacing tip: Dust and overspray looks right along the lower doors and the rear bumper, and Mud splatter behind the wheel arches. This is colour only. Add the dirty-gloss with the Wear Brush in the Material / Spec menu so the spec map matches.
Taper out gives clean racing-stripe swooshes. For a straight tapered stripe, click once, then Shift-click the end point.
Two-tone flecks uses your Foreground and Background colours, so set them to the sponsor colours first.
pitfalls: Dynamics is for the Brush (the layer Brush, and the zone mask brush in ZONE mode). It does not change the Eraser. In ZONE mode the colour sliders are dimmed, because a zone is a mask and has no colour.
Presets can change Spacing or Hardness. If a stroke looks different afterwards, look at the brush bar.

deep.heading: What a dab is
deep.body: A brush stroke is a row of round stamps called dabs. A normal brush stamps identical dabs exactly on the line. Brush Dynamics turns each stamp into one to eight dabs with their own size, position, strength and colour, so the stroke looks sprayed, speckled or hand made. Every extra dab goes through the same path as a normal stroke, so opacity, selection clipping and undo behave as usual. With Mirror Paint on, the mirrored side is a mirror image of the same stroke.

deep.heading: Taper
deep.body: Taper length is the distance over which the brush shrinks to a point. Taper end size is how small it gets (0 is a point). Grow instead of shrink starts the stroke as a point, and Fade the paint too makes the paint fainter along the taper. Taper out and Taper in are presets for these. A Shift-click straight line keeps the taper.

deep.heading: Presets and what they set
deep.body: Natural hand adds tiny random changes in size and strength. Speckle throws small flecks. Mud splatter throws big and small blobs wide. Dust and overspray makes a soft cloud. Confetti uses random hues. Two-tone flecks mixes your Foreground and Background colours. Several presets also set Spacing (and sometimes Hardness) for the best result, and the toast says which.

articles.title: Sponsor Kit (Car menu)
articles.summary: The Sponsor Kit (Car > Sponsor Kit...) cleans one picture and places it on every panel you tick. Add Sponsor Kit makes one layer per panel, and one Undo takes the whole kit back.
articles.what: The Sponsor Kit is in the Car menu, right under Number Kit. Give it one logo (a PNG, JPG or SVG file, or a layer you already have). It does three jobs. It takes the white or flat box off the logo, and the dirty fringe a JPEG leaves. It works out where this car can hold a logo (doors, rear quarters, TV panels, hood, trunk deck, roof rails). And it puts a copy on each part you tick, turned so it reads right on the car, and the same real size in centimetres on every part. You get one normal layer per part, linked as one kit. Nothing on the car moves until you drop a logo, and Cancel or Esc leaves the car exactly as it was.
when: You want the Sponsor Kit to put one logo on several panels of the car in one go.
You want the Sponsor Kit to clean a logo that came with a white box around it.
You want every Sponsor Kit copy to be the same real size on the car.
how: 1. Open the Car menu in the tool band and choose Sponsor Kit.... Nothing on the car moves yet.
2. Drop your logo on the box, or press Choose File... (PNG, JPG or SVG). If the logo is already a layer, select that layer and press Use Selected Layer.

3. Look at Before and After. Remove Box takes the box off. If it picked the wrong colour, click the box in the Before picture. Raise Edge if some fringe is left, lower Tolerance if part of the logo went missing, and leave Clear Inside off if white letters turn into holes.
4. Tick the parts with the Slots chips: Left Door, Right Door, Hood, Trunk / Deck, Left or Right Rear Quarter, Left or Right TV Panel, Left or Right Roof Rail.
5. Drag Size. The line under it shows the real size in centimetres on each part. Open Sizes and Turns on This Car to see room warnings or to add an Extra Turn.
6. Pick a Material if you want one: None, Chrome Foil, Gold Leaf, Gold Foil (solid), Matte Vinyl or Gloss Vinyl.
7. Press Add Sponsor Kit. Ctrl+Z takes the whole kit back in one step. To change it later, select one of its layers and open Sponsor Kit... again. Remove Kit deletes every layer of the kit at once.
tips: A wide logo suits a door, a square badge suits the rear quarter and a tall one suits the TV panel.
Drag one kit layer and only that part moves. The others stay where they are.
Gold Foil (solid) is the best gold for lettering. Gold Leaf is patchy on purpose and keeps the logo colours.
pitfalls: If the dialog says "Bigger than the room on...", the logo would run over the edge of that part. Lower Size or untick the part.
Chrome Foil and the gold materials change the shine in the spec map, not just the colour. Look at them in the Shine Lens before you render.
The kit puts copies on the car you have open. If you change the car template, add the kit again.
The kit keeps logos clear of Number Kit numbers: a logo moves to the nearest free spot on its part and shrinks if it must; the note says what moved. A logo you moved yourself stays put.

deep.heading: Real size, not a percentage
deep.body: Size is not a percent of the panel. The kit measures this car and shows the real size in centimetres under the slider, so a 30 cm logo is 30 cm on the door and 30 cm on the hood. A part that cannot hold that size is flagged with "Bigger than the room on...". The measuring is done once per car, so the numbers on a truck are different from the numbers on a stock car.

deep.heading: What Remove Box does
deep.body: It finds the box colour from the edge of the picture, removes it with the fringe a JPEG leaves, and keeps the logo colours. Click the box in the Before picture to choose the colour yourself; Auto Colour forgets that choice. Clear Inside also removes boxed-in areas of the same colour, such as the white inside letters, so leave it off for white lettering. A picture that already has a see-through background is left alone.

deep.heading: The six materials
deep.body: None keeps the shine the panel already has. Chrome Foil is mirror metal in the spec map (red 255, green 2, blue 16). Gold Leaf lays gold in sheets over the logo colours, so it is patchy by design. Gold Foil (solid) covers the whole logo with gold and is best for lettering. Matte Vinyl and Gloss Vinyl set a flat or a glossy finish under the logo.

faq.a: A dialog in the Car menu that cleans one logo and places it on the car parts you tick, turned right and the same real size on each.

faq.q: Where is the Sponsor Kit?
faq.a: Open the Car menu in the tool band and choose Sponsor Kit.... It sits right under Number Kit.

faq.q: How do I use the Sponsor Kit?
faq.a: Drop a logo on the box, tick the parts, set Size, pick a Material if you like, then press Add Sponsor Kit.

faq.q: Does the Sponsor Kit take the white box off my logo?
faq.a: Yes. Remove Box does that, and Before and After show the result. Click the box in Before if it picked the wrong colour.

faq.q: Can I undo the Sponsor Kit?
faq.a: Yes. One Ctrl+Z takes back the whole kit. Remove Kit in the dialog deletes all of its layers later.

faq.q: What are Gold Leaf and Gold Foil in the Sponsor Kit?
faq.a: Gold Leaf is gold laid in sheets over the logo colours and is patchy on purpose. Gold Foil (solid) covers the logo with plain gold and suits lettering.

faq.q: Does the Sponsor Kit survive saving the project?
faq.a: Yes. Save the project and open it again and the kit is still linked and editable.

mistakes.symptom: Sponsor Kit says Bigger than the room on a part
mistakes.cause: The size you chose is larger than that part can hold, so the logo would run over its edge.
mistakes.fix: Lower Size, or untick that part under Slots.

mistakes.symptom: Sponsor Kit left a box around the logo
mistakes.cause: It picked the wrong box colour, or the box is not one flat colour.
mistakes.fix: Click the box in the Before picture to choose its colour, then raise Tolerance a little.

mistakes.symptom: Sponsor Kit turned white letters into holes
mistakes.cause: Clear Inside removes boxed-in areas that match the box colour, and white letters count.
mistakes.fix: Leave Clear Inside off.

protips: Do the Sponsor Kit before the colours and effects on top of it. Then a later change of Size or Material updates every part in one move.

articles.title: Number Kit (Car menu)
articles.summary: The Number Kit (Car > Number Kit...) puts your car number on the left door, the right door and the roof in one go, each turned to read right on the car. Add Number Kit keeps them as normal layers, and one Undo takes the whole kit back.
articles.what: The Number Kit is in the Car menu. Type the car number once (1 to 4 letters or digits) and the three numbers appear on the car right away: Left Door, Right Door and Roof. Each one is turned to read the right way on the car, because one side of the car is upside down on the flat sheet. You choose the look once (font, Bold, Italic, Slant, Gap, Fill, two outlines, a shadow and an optional number panel) and every place updates together. If the paint already has numbers on its Numbers layer the dialog tells you and asks whether to replace them. Esc or Cancel takes the live numbers off and changes nothing.
when: You want the Number Kit to put the same car number on both doors and the roof.
You want to change the Number Kit look once and have every number follow.
You want the Number Kit to replace the numbers the paint already has.
how: 1. Open the paint with its car template, then open Car > Number Kit....
2. Type the number. It appears on the car at once: Left Door, Right Door and Roof.
3. Pick the look: Font, Bold, Italic, Slant, Gap, Fill, Outline 1, Outline 2 (colour and thickness in percent of the number size, 0 is none), Shadow and Panel.
4. Under Places, switch Left Door, Right Door and Roof on or off. Roof says which side it reads from (Reads From Driver’s Side is the usual choice). Size scales all three.
5. Pick a Material if you want one: None, Chrome Foil, Gloss Vinyl, Satin Vinyl or Matte Vinyl. It goes into the spec map with the number.
6. If the paint already has numbers, choose Replace Existing (the new number takes the old height, centre and slant), Add Alongside, or Cancel.
7. Press Add Number Kit. One Ctrl+Z takes the whole kit back, and Ctrl+Y brings it back exactly.
tips: Each number is a normal layer afterwards. Move, hide, change opacity or blend any one of them.
To change the number later, click it with the Text tool, or select one of its layers and open Number Kit... again. Every place updates and any place you moved stays where you put it.
Re-Centre puts every number back in its default spot. Remove Kit deletes all of its layers in one step.
pitfalls: If Sim-Stamped Number is on in the Car group, iRacing stamps its own number over yours. Press Use Custom Number in the warning to turn that off.
A number that runs past the edge of a panel is cut off there. Lower Size if the digits touch the edge.
Chrome Foil changes the shine in the spec map, not only the colour. Check it in the Shine Lens.
aliases: how do i use the number kit
what does the number kit do

deep.heading: Why three numbers turn differently
deep.body: The paint is the car cut open and laid flat, so the left door, the right door and the roof sit at different turns on the sheet, and the right side is upside down. The Number Kit measures the car, turns each number to read right on the car, and keeps that when you change the look. Roof says which side the roof number reads from. Turn Each Place lets you override one place on an odd car.

deep.heading: Replace Existing or Add Alongside
deep.body: When the Numbers layer of the paint already has numbers, the dialog says so. Replace Existing erases them where the kit goes and the new number takes their height, centre and slant, so Size 100% matches the old numbers. Type your own Slant to override that. Add Alongside keeps the old numbers. Cancel takes the kit back.

deep.heading: Saved with the project
deep.body: Saving the project keeps the kit data, so the numbers stay editable after you open it again. If you are on the Text tool, a click on a kit number re-opens the kit.

examples.goal: One dialog, three places
examples.result: Three number layers, each reading right on the car.

examples.title: Chrome numbers with a shadow
examples.goal: Mirror-metal digits that stand off the paint
examples.result: Chrome in the spec map under the number, with a soft shadow.

faq.q: What is the Number Kit?
faq.a: A dialog in the Car menu that puts your car number on the left door, right door and roof at once, each turned to read right.

faq.q: Where is the Number Kit?
faq.a: Open the Car menu in the tool band and choose Number Kit....

faq.q: How do I use the Number Kit?
faq.a: Type the number, pick the look and the places, then press Add Number Kit. Esc or Cancel changes nothing.

faq.q: What do Replace Existing and Add Alongside do in the Number Kit?
faq.a: Replace Existing erases the old numbers where the kit goes and copies their height, centre and slant. Add Alongside keeps them.

faq.q: Why does the Number Kit say Sim-Stamped Number is on?
faq.a: iRacing stamps its own number over your paint when that setting is on. Press Use Custom Number to switch to your own.

faq.q: How do I remove the Number Kit?
faq.a: Open the kit again and press Remove Kit, or press Ctrl+Z straight after adding it.

faq.q: What font and outline choices does the Number Kit have?
faq.a: Font, Bold, Italic, Slant and Gap for the letters, then Fill, Outline 1, Outline 2 and Shadow for the colours, and an optional Panel behind the number. Every place on the car updates together.

mistakes.symptom: Number Kit numbers are covered in iRacing
mistakes.cause: Sim-Stamped Number is on, so iRacing stamps its own number over yours.
mistakes.fix: Press Use Custom Number in the warning of the dialog.

mistakes.symptom: Number Kit did not keep my old numbers
mistakes.cause: Replace Existing is the default when the paint already has numbers.
mistakes.fix: Choose Add Alongside, or press Ctrl+Z and add the kit again.

mistakes.symptom: Number Kit roof number reads the wrong way
mistakes.cause: The roof reads from the opposite side to the one you expect.
mistakes.fix: Change Roof to Reads From Passenger’s Side, or set a Turn for the Roof under Turn Each Place.

protips: Type the number first and look at the car, then spend time on the look. Everything updates live, and Esc puts it all back if you do not like it.

articles.title: Spec Doctor (Material / Spec menu)
articles.summary: Spec Doctor (Material / Spec > Spec Doctor) renders your spec map at full size, lists the mistakes that make iRacing paints look wrong, shows where each one is and fixes it with one click. It never changes anything until you click a fix.
articles.what: Spec Doctor checks the same spec map that RENDER writes. Open Material / Spec > Spec Doctor (on a narrow window the menus fold into Menus > Material / Spec, and it is also in the MASK > Advanced spec utilities) and press Run Check. It renders your car at full size, which takes about 20 to 40 seconds, and then lists every problem as a card: how serious it is (High, Medium or Tip), what it is, where it is (by car part, such as left side or hood), and why it matters in iRacing. A clean car shows "Nothing to fix". Spec Doctor gives no score. Designed looks such as holo, glitter, flake and Truchet are left alone.
when: You want Spec Doctor to check the spec map before you upload the paint to iRacing.
The car looks wrong in iRacing (black chrome, hazy gloss, sparkle at a distance) and you want Spec Doctor to find out why.
You want Spec Doctor to show the exact pixels of a problem on the Live Preview.
how: 1. Open Material / Spec > Spec Doctor. A small panel opens next to the Live Preview.
2. Press Run Check and wait 20 to 40 seconds while it renders the car.
3. Read the cards. Each one says how serious it is, what it is, where it is and why it matters.
4. Press Show on a card to draw a magenta heat overlay on the Live Preview over the exact pixels. Press it again to hide it.
5. Press the fix button on the card if you agree. Every fix is one undo step, so Ctrl+Z puts it back exactly.
6. Spec Doctor checks again after a fix and tells you if the problem is gone. Ignore hides a card, and Show Ignored at the bottom brings it back.
tips: Press Show first, look at where the pixels are, and only then press the fix.
If a card is a deliberate look (a dull coat on purpose), press Ignore. It will not nag again until you press Show Ignored.
Run Check again after any big change to the finishes, because it checks the current spec map, not a saved one.
pitfalls: Spec Doctor never changes anything by itself. If a fix button was not pressed, nothing moved.
The check renders at full size, so it takes longer than a normal preview. Wait for the result before you judge it.
It checks the spec map RENDER would write. Turn on the layers and zones you want in the render first.
aliases: how do i use spec doctor
spec doctor chrome over near black paint
spec doctor dull coat on a mirror smooth area
spec doctor decal layer took the body chrome

deep.heading: The eight things it looks for
deep.body: Chrome Over Near-Black Paint (iRacing chrome reflects the paint colour, so it turns into a black hole). Clearcoat Set To 1-15 (blue 1 to 15 means no clearcoat in iRacing, not a light coat). Dull Coat On A Mirror-Smooth Area (blue runs backwards: 16 is the glossiest, 255 the dullest). No Clearcoat Anywhere (a tip: fine for raw or matte builds, not for a gloss job). (Decal Layer) Took The Body’s Chrome (stickers over a chrome panel become chrome stickers). One Material On The Whole Car (a tip). Spec Sits N px Off The Paint (halos at the edges). Pixel Noise In Roughness / Metallic (sparkle that crawls at a distance).

deep.heading: What each fix does
deep.body: Chrome over near-black paint: lighten the paint under it, or make it a proper dark chrome. Clearcoat 1-15: keep it full gloss (16). Dull coat on a mirror: set clearcoat to 16. Decal took the chrome: give that decal layer Gloss Vinyl or Matte Vinyl. One material on the whole car: it offers two or three presets and applies nothing unless you click one. Spec off the paint: snap the zone mask back, or move the spec into line. Pixel noise: soften only that area.

deep.heading: Show and Ignore
deep.body: Show draws a magenta overlay on the Live Preview over the exact pixels of the problem, so you see which part of the car it is. Ignore hides a card for this check, and Show Ignored at the bottom brings the hidden cards back.

examples.goal: Catch the usual spec mistakes
examples.result: A list of cards, or "Nothing to fix".

examples.title: Find why chrome looks like a black hole
examples.goal: See where chrome sits over dark paint
examples.result: The magenta overlay marks the dark-painted chrome on the Live Preview.

faq.q: What is Spec Doctor?
faq.a: A check in the Material / Spec menu that looks for common spec map mistakes, shows where they are and offers a one-click fix.

faq.q: Where is Spec Doctor?
faq.a: Open the Material / Spec menu in the tool band and choose Spec Doctor. It is also in MASK > Advanced spec utilities, and under Menus > Material on a narrow window.

faq.q: How do I use Spec Doctor?
faq.a: Press Run Check, read the cards, press Show to see where a problem is, and press the fix button if you agree.

faq.q: What does Spec Doctor check?
faq.a: Chrome over near-black paint, clearcoat set to 1-15, a dull coat on a mirror-smooth area, no clearcoat anywhere, decals that took the body chrome, one material everywhere, a spec that sits off the paint and pixel noise.

faq.q: Does Spec Doctor change my paint by itself?
faq.a: No. Nothing changes until you press a fix button, and every fix is one Ctrl+Z.

faq.q: Why does Spec Doctor take so long?
faq.a: It renders the car at full size, the same spec map RENDER writes, which takes about 20 to 40 seconds.

faq.q: How do I hide a Spec Doctor card I do not want to fix?
faq.a: Press Ignore on the card. It goes away until you press Show Ignored. Nothing changes on the car either way.

mistakes.symptom: Spec Doctor says Chrome Over Near-Black Paint
mistakes.cause: Mirror chrome sits over very dark paint. iRacing chrome reflects the paint colour, so it looks like a black hole or plain gloss black.
mistakes.fix: Lighten the paint under the chrome, or use a proper dark chrome.

mistakes.symptom: Spec Doctor says Clearcoat Set To 1-15
mistakes.cause: In iRacing blue 1 to 15 means no clearcoat at all, not a light coat.
mistakes.fix: Keep it at 16 (full gloss) with the fix button.

mistakes.symptom: Spec Doctor says Nothing to fix but the car looks wrong
mistakes.cause: The problem is in the colour or the placement, not in the spec map. Designed looks are not flagged.
mistakes.fix: Check the colours and zones, and look at the car in the Shine Lens.

protips: Run Spec Doctor last, after your finishes and zones are done and before you upload. It is the quickest way to catch the mistakes that only show on the track.

articles.title: Car-Space Fade (Car menu)
articles.summary: Car-Space Fade (Car > Car-Space Fade...) fades colour and shine along the real car, nose to tail, bottom to top or centre out. Both sides match, the hood, roof and trunk carry on into one another, and decals stay on top.
articles.what: A normal gradient runs across the flat paint sheet, but the sheet is the car cut open, so a sheet gradient does not match the real car: the two sides differ and the hood, roof and trunk can run backwards. Car-Space Fade fades along the CAR instead. Choose Nose → Tail and the nose is the start and the tail the end on every part at once. Colour and material fade together, so you can go from chrome at the nose to matte at the tail. Open Car > Car-Space Fade.... A small panel opens and the fade is drawn on the sheet as you change it. Numbers, sponsors, logos and the Car Mandatory layer stay on top while Keep decals on top is ticked, which it is by default.
when: You want Car-Space Fade to make both sides of the car fade the same way.
You want Car-Space Fade to fade the shine as well as the colour, such as chrome at the nose into matte at the tail.
You want Car-Space Fade to run one fade across the hood, roof and trunk.
how: 1. Open Car > Car-Space Fade.... A panel opens. Nothing in the editor moves.

2. Pick a Direction: Nose → Tail, Bottom → Top, Centre → Out or Custom. For Custom press Pick 2 points, click where the fade starts and where it ends, and drag the two dots to adjust. Reverse swaps the two ends.
3. Parts: all parts are on. Click a part name to take it out (leave the bumpers alone, for example). Spread over: Chosen parts runs the fade from the first to the last of the parts you chose.

4. Stops: you start with two. Click the bar to see them, drag a stop to move it, press + Stop to add a third. Each stop has a colour and a material (Keep, Gloss, Satin, Matte, Chrome or Finish... for any finish in the catalogue). Untick Colour to fade only the material.
5. Look at the car. The fade is drawn on the sheet while the panel is open.
6. Press Add Fade. It shows in the Live Preview and the Shine Lens and is written by a normal RENDER exactly as you saw it. Reopen the panel to edit or remove a fade. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work.
tips: Chrome nose to matte tail: Nose → Tail, untick Colour, stop 1 material Chrome, stop 2 material Matte. The paint stays and the shine fades.
Sunset hood to roof to trunk: Nose → Tail, three stops (gold, red, deep purple), Colour on, material Keep.
Rocker glow: Bottom → Top, two stops, the first strong and the second the car’s own colour.
pitfalls: Bottom → Top is nearly flat on the roof, hood and trunk, because those three sit at almost the same height. Use Nose → Tail or Centre → Out for them.
A Finish... stop uses the finish’s own look, not the swatch colour. The sheet preview only tints it; the Live Preview shows the real thing.

Fades are saved inside your project file and come back when you open it, exactly as they were (a message says how many were restored); a project saved without fades opens with none. They are included in every render.

what does car space fade do
car space fade nose to tail
car space fade keep decals on top

deep.heading: Why a sheet gradient does not match the car
deep.body: The paint sheet is the car cut open and laid flat. A gradient that runs left to right on the sheet gives the left side and the right side different results, and runs the hood, roof and trunk the opposite way from the doors. Car-Space Fade measures the car and fades along the real body, so both sides come out essentially identical and the hood, roof and trunk carry on into one another.

deep.heading: Keep decals on top
deep.body: A fade replaces the paint inside the parts you fade. With Keep decals on top ticked (the default) the fade goes under numbers, sponsors, logos and the Car Mandatory layer, like a stripe laid on the base paint, and the decals stay exactly as they are, with a half-strength ring around their edges so soft edges stay soft. Untick it to let the fade cover everything inside the parts. Hidden layers are not protected, because they are not in the render.

deep.heading: Direction choices
deep.body: Nose → Tail starts at the front and ends at the back. Bottom → Top starts at the sills and ends at the roof. Centre → Out starts on the centre line (hood, roof, trunk) and ends at the sills and bumper edges. Custom lets you click any two points on the car. Spread over: Whole car runs the fade end to end of the car, and Chosen parts runs it end to end of just the parts you picked.

examples.result: The paint stays and the shine fades from mirror to flat along the whole car.

faq.q: What is Car-Space Fade?
faq.a: A fade that runs along the real car instead of the flat sheet, so both sides match and the hood, roof and trunk carry on into one another.

faq.q: Where is Car-Space Fade?
faq.a: Open the Car menu in the tool band and choose Car-Space Fade....

faq.q: How do I use Car-Space Fade?
faq.a: Pick a Direction, choose the parts, set the stops (colour and material), then press Add Fade.

faq.q: How is Car-Space Fade different from the Gradient tool?
faq.a: The Gradient tool runs across the flat sheet, so the two sides and the top row can come out different. Car-Space Fade runs along the car and also fades the shine.

faq.q: What does Keep decals on top do in Car-Space Fade?
faq.a: It keeps numbers, sponsors, logos and the Car Mandatory layer exactly as they are and puts the fade under them. It is on by default.

faq.q: Can Car-Space Fade fade the shine as well as the colour?
faq.a: Yes. Each stop has a colour and a material. Untick Colour to fade only the material.

faq.q: How do I add stops and colours to a Car-Space Fade?
faq.a: Drag a stop along the bar or press + Stop to add one. Each stop has its own colour and material, so a fade can run from red gloss at the nose to black matte at the tail.

mistakes.symptom: Car-Space Fade covers my numbers and sponsors
mistakes.cause: Keep decals on top is unticked, or the layers are hidden or not recognised as numbers, sponsors or logos.
mistakes.fix: Tick Keep decals on top, or take those parts out of the Parts list.

mistakes.symptom: Car-Space Fade Bottom → Top does nothing on the roof
mistakes.cause: The hood, roof and trunk sit at almost the same height.
mistakes.fix: Use Nose → Tail or Centre → Out for those parts.

mistakes.symptom: Car-Space Fade is missing after opening a project
mistakes.cause: The project was saved before the fade was added, or the fade could not line up with the car (the open message says so).
mistakes.fix: Add the fade again with Add Fade, then save the project again.

protips: Drag a stop around freely: the preview draws at lower detail while you drag and settles to full detail a moment after you let go.

articles.title: Auto Spec: a first spec for the whole car in one click
articles.summary: Auto Spec (Material / Spec > Auto Spec...) reads every layer of your car and proposes a believable material for each one, with a Showroom to Race-Worn dial. Apply Auto Spec gives each ticked layer its material in one undo step and never touches your paint.
articles.what: Most paints never get a proper spec map, because it is a second painting done blind in grey channels. Auto Spec does the first draft. It looks at each printed layer (its name, its pixels and which car parts it sits on), works out what it is (body paint, numbers, sponsor decals, tape, silver art, black trim, carbon) and proposes one real material for it. You check the list, change anything you like and apply. It only picks materials that already exist and never uses the protected finishes. It needs layers: a car that is one flat picture has nothing to read, so use the zones or the Spec Brush for that.
when: You want Auto Spec to give every layer of the car a sensible material in one go.
You want to see Auto Spec’s proposal under the Shine Lens before anything is final.
You want a first spec draft that you then fine-tune by hand.
how: 1. Open the Material / Spec menu in the tool band and choose Auto Spec.... A window opens next to the Live Preview and reads your layers (a few seconds).

2. Read the list. Each row is one layer: a tick box, its name (click it to select that layer), a Material box, what it thinks the layer is, the parts it sits on, a percent and one sentence saying why. Now and Proposed show the spec numbers (M metallic, R roughness, C clearcoat).
3. Change any Material box you disagree with. Leave To The Zones keeps the zone’s own finish for that layer.
4. Drag the Showroom to Race-Worn dial. Showroom is glossy with mirror chrome, the middle is the default, Race-Worn is satin and matte vinyl with a little grain. Materials you set yourself stay put.
5. Keep Live Preview ticked to see the proposal under the Shine Lens. Rescan reads the layers again.
6. Press Apply Auto Spec. Every ticked layer gets its Layer Material in one undo step: Ctrl+Z takes it all back. Cancel puts everything back exactly.
7. Spec Doctor then checks the whole spec by itself. With Doctor fixes ticked it also repairs any high problem it finds.
tips: Rows that are already right, rows marked Not sure, template layers and tiny specks start unticked.
pitfalls: A layer that already has a Layer Material is left alone unless you tick it.
The proposal is a first draft by rule. Look at the rows before you apply.
aliases: how do i use auto spec
auto spec leave to the zones

deep.heading: What it reads and the dial
deep.body: For each layer it looks at the name, the pixels and which car parts the layer covers. The percent is how well those agree; under 60 percent is marked Not sure and starts unticked. Showroom puts gel-coat clearcoat on decals and mirror chrome on silver art. The middle puts gloss vinyl on sponsors and satin on numbers, tape and black trim. Race-Worn gives satin paint, matte vinyl and brushed metal with a little grain.

deep.heading: What Apply changes
deep.body: Only the spec of the ticked layers, as Layer Materials. Your artwork, zones and colours are not touched. It is one undo step, and Spec Doctor runs right after.

examples.title: A first spec for a finished livery
examples.goal: Give every layer a sensible material
examples.result: Numbers get satin, sponsor decals gloss vinyl, silver art hazy chrome, and the Spec Doctor line says the spec is clean.

faq.q: What is Auto Spec?
faq.a: A window in the Material / Spec menu that reads every layer and proposes a believable material for each one, which you check and apply in one step.

faq.q: Where is Auto Spec?
faq.a: Open the Material / Spec menu in the tool band and choose Auto Spec.... It sits in the Whole Car group, under Layer Materials.

faq.q: How do I use Auto Spec?
faq.a: Open it, check the rows, change any Material box you want, drag the Showroom to Race-Worn dial, then press Apply Auto Spec.

faq.q: Can I undo Auto Spec?
faq.a: Yes. One Ctrl+Z takes back the whole thing. Cancel puts everything back before you apply.

faq.q: Does Auto Spec change my paint colours?
faq.a: No. Only the spec of the ticked layers changes.

mistakes.symptom: Auto Spec finds no layers
mistakes.cause: The car is one flat picture or a template with only guide layers.
mistakes.fix: Open the layered paint, or set the shine with the zones and the Spec Brush.
